findings.title: Pre-Vote responses of an earlier round are accepted by a later round of the same term
findings.summary: Engine::pre_elect builds every Pre-Vote round from the unchanged local vote, so all rounds at one local term share the leader id (term+1, self). RaftCore::does_pre_candidate_vote_match only compares leader ids, so a response to an earlier round (timer restart, operator trigger, or a round dropped by leader contact) is counted by the current round. The counterexample starts two timer rounds and completes the second with a grant issued for the first. If the membership changed between the rounds so that the responder is no longer a voter, Candidate::grant_by panics (expect "target not in quorum set") and RaftCore stops; otherwise a real election can start on grants the current round never obtained.

findings.title: A Pre-Vote round started while Candidate survives leader establishment; the new Leader starts another election
findings.summary: The election timer keeps firing for a Candidate and, with Pre-Vote enabled, starts a Pre-Vote round while the real election is still running. establish_leader does not drop Engine.pre_candidate, and handle_pre_vote_resp calls elect() on quorum without checking the node's role, so when the round's grants arrive the freshly established Leader starts an election at term+1 and steps down. do_elect keeps the stale leader object, tripping try_leader_handler's debug_assert (leader.vote >= state.vote) in debug builds. The same happens after trigger().elect(true) on a Candidate.
